SECTION I  STANDARD CONSULTATION FEES

GENERAL PRACTITIONER / FAMILY PHYSICIAN

IN-OFFICE CONSULTATION FEES
Short Consultation (0 to 10 minutes, per 1/6-minute block)  $20 - $30
Long Consultation (11 to 20 minutes, per 1/6-minute block)  $30 - $55
Very Long Consultation (21 to 30 minutes, per 1/6-minute block)  $40 - $75

OUT-OF-OFFICE CONSULTATION FEES
Telephone Consultation  $20 - $25
Home Visit  $20 - $30
Emergency Consultation  $20 - $30
Hospital Consultation  $20 - $30
Death Certification  $20 - $30

SPECIALIST

IN-OFFICE CONSULTATION FEES
Short Consultation (0 to 10 minutes, per 1/6-minute block)  $65 - $100
Long Consultation (11 to 20 minutes, per 1/6-minute block)  $90 - $150
Very Long Consultation (21 to 30 minutes, per 1/6-minute block)  $150 - $300

OUT-OF-OFFICE CONSULTATION FEES
Telephone Consultation  $50 - $250
Home Visit  $200 - $500
Emergency Consultation  $200 - $500
Hospital Consultation  $200 - $500
Death Certification  $200 - $500

1.2  CONSULTATION FEES DO NOT INCLUDE costs of medications, injections,
    dressings, special procedures, laboratory tests, other investigations (e.g. X-rays), etc.

1.3  SHORT CONSULTATION refers to a brief office visit for simple medical
    problems.  It does not include a detailed history, physical examination, or
    special investigations.  It is not appropriate for patients with complex
    problems, routine antenatal visits for healthy mothers or routine post-operative office
    visits.

1.4  LONG CONSULTATION refers to a consultation that is more complex and intensive
    than a short consultation.  It usually involves a detailed history, physical
    examination, special investigations, and/or counselling.  It is appropriate for
    patients with complex or multiple problems, patients with chronic diseases, and
    patients requiring counselling.  It is also appropriate for patients with
    long consultation / chronic conditions, quality is "long consultation".

1.5  OUT-OF-OFFICE CONSULTATION refers to a consultation where both the doctor and the
    patient are not at the usual office premises but at other locations, and
    includes telephone consultations, home visits, hospital visits, etc.  It is
    proposed that this form of charging for consultations which are likely to exceed 20
    minutes.

1.6  EMERGENCY CONSULTATION refers to cases requiring immediate attention and is
    required.  The emergency consultation fee is charged when the doctor is
    called out to attend to the patient outside the clinic.  Non-emergency / refers
    to cases that can be scheduled to a mutually opportune time.

1.7  HOSPITAL IN-PATIENT CONSULTATION (per day) refers to the number of visits the doctor
    makes to the patient in hospital.  The fee is charged for each day the doctor
    visits the patient, and it has to be contractible at any time or may be called
    back for any problem.

1.8  CLINIC VISIT CLAIM FORM
    Each clinic visit claim form contains the following:
    (a)  Patient's name, identity card number, age, sex, ID number and occupation.
    (b)  Date of consultation and diagnosis (see p. 9).
    (c)  The fee charged including breakdown of charges.
    (d)  The signature of the doctor and patient.

    This service is not chargeable if the form is passed on the same clinic visit or
    the same day.  The form is not chargeable if the patient is referred or
    discharged, the maximum is up to 35 consultations per week and there is a fee of
    $10 for each form.

1.9  PRESCRIPTION FEE FOR GENERAL PRACTITIONER AND SPECIALIST
    1)  Prescription fee is $10 per prescription.
    2)  Fee is not chargeable if the prescription is issued on the same clinic visit or
        request made on a separate visit or without consultation.  $10
